questions.query: During what acquisition period were the mammograms in this study obtained, and what average-measures ICC estimates and 95% confidence intervals were reported for the final BI-RADS assessment without and with AI?
questions.expected_answer: Mammography cases were from January 2021 to May 2022. Without AI the average-measures ICC was 0.910 (95% CI 0.894–0.924); with AI it was 0.931 (95% CI 0.920–0.941).

support_sets.quote: involving mammography cases from January 2021 to May 2022 done in Hospital Al-Sultan Abdullah UiTM.

Without AI software, the average measures ICC was 0.910 with a 95% CI of 0.894 to 0.924, F(433, 1299), p < 0.001. With AI software, the average measures ICC was 0.931 with a 95% CI of 0.920 to 0.941, F (433, 1299), p < 0.001.

questions.query: For this article's own final non-mass-lesion cohort, what sampling period and diagnostic-reference breakdown were reported, and, at a BI-RADS 4B cutoff, what sensitivity and specificity with the literal reported intervals appear in Results?
questions.expected_answer: Sampling was January 2017–December 2021. The final cohort was 59 women/59 US-detected non-mass lesions, with diagnoses based on surgical excision (n=52) or US-guided core needle biopsy (n=7). Results reports sensitivity 82.98% (69.19%–92.35%) and specificity 41.67% (15.17%–72.33%); the intervals are retained as printed without adding a confidence level.

support_sets.quote: between January 2017 and December 2021 in a tertiary hospital

Finally, 59 women (mean age 43.3 years ± 10.8, age, range 30–78years) with 59 US-detected breast NMLs were included, for which final diagnoses were established, basing on histopathologic results of surgical excision (n = 52) and US-guided core needle biopsy (n = 7).

If BI-RADS category 4B was taken as a cutoff value, the sensitivity, specificity, AUC, PPV, NPV, and OR were 82.98%(69.19%-92.35%), 41.67%(15.17%-72.33%), 0.62(0.49–0.75), 84.78%(71.13%-93.66%), 38.46%(13.86%-68.42%) and 3.48, respectively.
